config.title: React Server Components & SSR vs SSG

intro.title: React Server Components & SSR vs SSG
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple blog post page that demonstrates different rendering strategies in React. You will learn the core concepts of React Server Components (RSC), Server-Side Rendering (SSR), and Static Site Generation (SSG). The main technologies involved are React with TypeScript, using the 'use client' directive and the Next.js framework for server-side features. You'll see how to fetch data on the server and pre-render pages to improve performance and SEO. By the end, you'll understand when to use each approach for your web applications.
intro.usecase: React Server Components (RSCs) and SSR/SSG are foundational for building fast, SEO-friendly web applications like e-commerce product pages, news articles, and marketing sites. For example, an e-commerce site uses SSR to render product listings with real-time inventory and user reviews, ensuring search engines index the content while providing immediate interactivity. A content dashboard leverages RSCs to fetch and display analytics data on the server, reducing client-side JavaScript and improving load times for complex tables and charts. Developers implement SSG for blog posts or documentation sites, pre-rendering static pages at build time for instant delivery and global scalability.

objectives: Initialize a Next.js project with TypeScript to implement server-side rendering capabilities
Configure page components to use React Server Components by removing client-side hooks and effects
Construct a static page using Static Site Generation (SSG) with getStaticProps in TypeScript
Implement Server-Side Rendering (SSR) by applying getServerSideProps to fetch data at request time
Manipulate component rendering by controlling when to use client-side interactivity with the 'use client' directive
Integrate dynamic data fetching in server components while maintaining type safety with TypeScript interfaces
Render a hybrid application that combines static, server-rendered, and client-rendered components based on use case
